access.unit: ACCESS credit per Anvil CPU service unit (1 core-hour)
access.notes: Operations announcement: discounted rate effective 2024-11-19. Not logged in; documentation only.

access.unit: ACCESS credits per Anvil GPU-hour (A100) - APPROXIMATE, derived
access.notes: Derived from Purdue's example: 400,000 credits ~ 334,000 CPU core-h or ~6,000 GPU-h (1.2 credits/core-h pre-discount; 400000/6000 ~ 67). Not a published rate; the live exchange calculator (https://allocations.access-ci.org/exchange_calculator) is dynamic and its rates did not render. Anvil AI (H100) is a separate resource; rate not found.

access.unit: ACCESS credits per Delta GPU SU
access.notes: NOT FOUND: calculator rates not rendered. Unit definition: 1 Delta GPU SU = 1 A100 GPU-hour in quad-A100 partition (https://operations.access-ci.org/node/593); that page says H200 charge factor is 3x, whereas Delta docs (https://docs.ncsa.illinois.edu/systems/delta/en/latest/user_guide/job_accounting.html) say 1 SU/GPU-h for A100 and H200 and 1 SU per core-h CPU - sources disagree. H100 on Delta not listed (Delta has A100, A40, MI100, H200). Delta CPU listed separately.

h100_nvl_tdp.source_url: https://www.pny.com/File Library/Company/Support/Product Brochures/NVIDIA Data Center GPUs/english/H100-NVL-Datasheet.pdf
h100_nvl_tdp.notes: PNY datasheet (vendor reseller of NVIDIA); some resellers print '2x 350-400W' for the NVL pair. Passive PCIe 5.0, NVLink bridge.

gpu_server_wall_2x_h100_nvl.notes: No measured or vendor figure found. Back-of-envelope ESTIMATE ~1,200-1,600 W (2x400 W GPUs + dual-socket host/fans/PSU loss); central 1,400 W. For scale, a measured 8-GPU H100 SXM HGX node peaked ~8.4 kW vs 10.2 kW rated (https://arxiv.org/html/2412.08602v2).

cpu_server_wall_dual_socket_64core.notes: SPECpower_ssj2008, Lenovo ThinkSystem SR665 V3 results (630 W and 634 W average active power at 100%; found via search snippets, I did not open each file). ASUS RS720A-E12 dual-9654 results are 817-827 W. A 2x32-core box would be lower; SPECpower is a synthetic Java load, not alignment. Central 650 W.

us_electricity_price.unit: cents per kWh, US average, August 2026 (preliminary)
us_electricity_price.notes: EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.A, released 2026-10-23; August 2026 is the latest month.

pue.unit: ratio, global average of surveyed data centres, 2024
pue.notes: Uptime Institute 14th Global Data Center Survey (2024); the 1.56 figure came from a secondary summary (ashb.com), not verified in the Uptime PDF. Another low-quality site says 1.58. Hyperscale facilities are much lower (~1.1-1.2) but not sourced here.

third_party.unit: USD per 30x WGS sample, FASTQ to VCF
third_party.notes: THIRD-PARTY / vendor-adjacent claim (Terra blog on Parabricks); DNA germline, not RNA-seq/STAR; older GPU generation.

third_party.value: up to 50% lower compute cost for WGS vs CPU-only
third_party.notes: NVIDIA marketing claim as relayed by search result; not verified on the page.

third_party.unit: USD per RNA-seq sample (STAR vs rna_fq2bam)
third_party.notes: NVIDIA genomics page lists rna_fq2bam (STAR) runtimes in minutes by GPU config (e.g. 7.55 ... 22.28 min) but no cost and column headers were not captured. No cost-per-sample for RNA-seq found. A BMC Bioinformatics 2023 benchmark (PMID 37259021) reports GPU germline callers cheaper on AWS/GCP but some somatic callers costlier.
